advisory.finding: The new comments say an `expect: advisory` case is 'still held to the grounding scorers (`_cites_real_paths`)', but code-review-tests.eval.yaml lists no grounding scorer. Only code_review_emits_valid_findings, code_review_recall and code_review_no_fire are configured, and only the code-quality spec uses cites_real_paths. Recall and no-fire both skip the advisory case, so it is graded on output shape alone. A hallucinated or ungrounded finding on the guard-(vii) case still passes every epoch.
scenarios: On the guard-(vii) case the reviewer emits a made-up finding with no real path citation; the case still passes, because only the shape check applies.

Named violating input: case {expect: 'advisory', id: 'FP-preexisting-code-gap-no-new-behaviour'} with output {'findings': [{'claim': 'x', 'citations': []}]}. Under the code-review-tests spec's scorers, every applicable scorer passes, even though the stated contract says this ungrounded finding should be held to grounding.
advisory.finding: Nothing tests the promise that `expect: advisory` cases are 'still held to the grounding scorers', and the promise is false for the one spec that uses `advisory`. code-review-tests registers only the shape, recall and no-fire scorers, so on the advisory case only the shape scorer applies. A finding with no grounding passes every gating scorer, and no test catches this.
scenarios: The reviewer gives an ungrounded or made-up coverage-gap finding on the guard-(vii) case. The live eval scores the case as passing, so a regression into ungrounded findings on downgraded cases goes unnoticed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `cites_real_paths` (or an equivalent grounding scorer) to the code-review-tests spec's `scorers:` list. Add a unit test that loads the spec, takes the advisory case, and asserts that at least one registered deterministic scorer is applicable and fails on an uncited finding, e.g. `sc.score('cites_real_paths', advisory_case, {'findings': [{'claim': 'x', 'citations': []}]}).passed is False`.
